name: org.machanism.machai:machai-mcp-server
description: Machai MCP Server is a Java 17 Model Context Protocol server for publishing Machai AI functional tools and prompts to MCP-compatible clients. It is an orchestration and transport artifact, not a bundle of domain tools: deployers add Machai-compatible functional-tool and prompt libraries to the runtime classpath, then the server discovers and exposes their capabilities. The org.machanism.machai.mcp.server.McpServer command-line entry point defaults to local STDIO transport and starts an HTTP endpoint when given a port. HTTP deployments support stateless and streamable session-oriented transports. The server adapts functional-tool metadata and parameters to MCP tool schemas, routes invocations to the registered functions, passes an optional project directory as execution context, exposes prompts, and propagates MCP session identifiers where available. It is intended for Java-based generative-AI automation, developer tooling, remote tool gateways, and integrations with MCP clients such as Claude Desktop and MCP Inspector.

usageContext: Expose Machai functional tools and prompts to MCP-compatible AI clients
Launch a local MCP process that communicates over standard input and output
Host a remote MCP endpoint over HTTP using stateless or streamable transport
Supply a configured project directory to runtime tool execution
Bridge independently packaged Java AI tools into desktop clients, inspectors, and automation agents

constructors.description: Creates the MCP server application entry-point object. Production startup is normally performed by the static main method, which chooses STDIO or HTTP server implementations from command-line options.

examples.description: Creates the entry-point object for a Java integration. Invoke org.machanism.machai.mcp.server.McpServer.main(java.lang.String[]) for normal command-line startup.

constructors.description: Creates an HTTP MCP server implementation that uses stateless transport and reports the supplied server name and version to MCP clients.

examples.description: Creates a stateless HTTP server programmatically and configures its listening port. Tool registration must be completed before the server is started.

constructors.description: Creates an HTTP MCP server implementation that uses streamable, session-oriented MCP transport and reports the supplied identity to clients.

examples.description: Creates a streamable HTTP server programmatically for clients that need session-aware MCP communication.

features.name: main
features.signature: public static void main(java.lang.String[] args) throws java.lang.Exception
features.description: Parses the CLI and starts the MCP server. With no port option, it runs a STDIO server. With --port, it runs HTTP; adding --session selects streamable HTTP, otherwise the HTTP server is stateless. It accepts --projectDir, --name, --config, and --version to configure the server before tool discovery and startup.

examples.description: Step 1: install the server from Maven Central or build it with mvn clean package. Step 2: put the server JAR and a Machai-compatible functional-tool container JAR on the Java classpath. Step 3: run this command without --port for STDIO. Step 4: configure the local MCP client to launch this command, then invoke the discovered tools. Use a colon rather than a semicolon as the classpath separator on Unix-like systems.

Step 1: install the server and tool container JARs on a Java 17 runtime. Step 2: start a streamable HTTP endpoint on port 45000. Step 3: connect an MCP-compatible client or bridge to http://localhost:45000/mcp and test tool discovery.

features.name: getConfigurator
features.signature: public static org.machanism.macha.core.commons.configurator.PropertiesConfigurator getConfigurator(java.lang.String configFile) throws java.io.IOException
features.description: Creates a properties configurator and loads an explicit configuration path, or the default mcp.properties file when the argument is null. A missing default file is tolerated; an unreadable explicit file causes java.io.IOException.

examples.description: Loads a readable explicit properties file for server-related configuration. Handle java.io.IOException when the explicit path may be unavailable.

features.name: toHumanReadable
features.description: Converts camelCase, snake_case, or kebab-case tool names into a title-style display name used for MCP tool metadata. Null and empty input produce an empty string.

examples.description: Produces Search Project Files, making a machine-oriented functional-tool name clearer in an MCP client interface.

features.name: setProjectDir
features.description: Sets the project directory passed to server tools as their execution context. A null directory permits request-specific resolution.

examples.description: Sets a fixed working project context for tools exposed by a programmatically created HTTP server.

features.name: setPort
features.description: Configures the TCP port used by an HTTP MCP server before it is started with its configured servlet transport provider.

examples.description: Configures port 45000 for a streamable HTTP MCP server before registration and startup.

customizations.name: Command-line server configuration
customizations.description: Customize startup with --name, --version, --projectDir, --config, --port, and --session. --port changes the default STDIO deployment to HTTP, and --session selects streamable transport only in HTTP mode. The default server name is mcp-machai-server; the version defaults to package implementation metadata or latest.

examples.description: Starts a stateless HTTP MCP endpoint with explicit identity and properties configuration. Configure an MCP client to use http://localhost:45000/mcp.

customizations.name: enabledTools
customizations.description: The enabledTools configuration property limits publication to named tools. Its value may separate tool names using spaces, commas, semicolons, or other whitespace. When it is not configured, the server does not apply this restriction.

examples.description: Add this property to the configuration file passed with --config to expose only the listed discovered tools.

customizations.name: Runtime functional-tool and prompt libraries
customizations.description: Deploy Machai-compatible implementations of org.machanism.machai.process.tools.FunctionTools and prompt providers in separate JARs with their required service-provider registration. Put those JARs on the runtime classpath to have the server discover and publish their MCP capabilities without modifying this artifact.

examples.description: Package custom tools with their required service-provider registration, add the custom JAR alongside the server JAR, start the endpoint, then verify registered tools with MCP Inspector.

studs.name: org.machanism.machai.mcp.server.AbstractMcpServer
studs.description: Common MCP-server boundary for transport implementations. It holds project-directory context and defines package-level tool registration and server startup hooks.

examples.description: Use a concrete STDIO or HTTP implementation through the common abstract server type when configuring shared project context.

studs.name: org.machanism.machai.mcp.server.AbstractHttpMcpServer
studs.description: HTTP-specific MCP-server boundary that provides Jetty port and servlet transport-provider configuration for concrete stateless and streamable servers.

examples.description: Configure an HTTP MCP implementation through its common HTTP abstraction before startup.

examples.title: Install, configure, and run a local STDIO MCP server
steps: Install Java 17 or newer and obtain org.machanism.machai:machai-mcp-server:1.4.2 from Maven Central, or build the project with mvn clean package.
Obtain or build a Machai-compatible functional-tool container JAR with its required service-provider registration.
Place both JARs on the Java runtime classpath and configure an MCP desktop client to start org.machanism.machai.mcp.server.McpServer.
Start the client. It launches the process through STDIO, discovers its tools and prompts, and can invoke the published capabilities.

examples.title: Run and test a remote streamable HTTP MCP endpoint
steps: Install Java 17 or newer, the server JAR, and a functional-tool container JAR on the host.
Set environment variables, credentials, model settings, and other configuration required by the selected tools.
Run the fully qualified server entry point with --port and --session.
Install or run MCP Inspector with npx @modelcontextprotocol/inspector, connect it to http://localhost:45000/mcp, and validate tool discovery and invocation.

examples.title: Configure Claude Desktop for a STDIO deployment
steps: Install the server JAR and the functional-tool container JAR on the desktop machine.
Add the command configuration to the MCP client settings, using the Java executable, classpath, and fully qualified org.machanism.machai.mcp.server.McpServer class.
Add required tool environment variables to the client configuration without embedding secrets in source control.
Restart the client and select an exposed tool to verify the integration.
